title: Low Effort Show and Tell - Episode 2
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v_JJzLJ0eRw

Daniel (@dungeondive) runs a second Low Effort Show and Tell, and this haul leans hard towards solo RPGs.

The one he is most excited about is Disciples of Bone and Shadow in the Conquered Sun edition — a genuinely all-in-one solo RPG with dungeon crawling, hex crawling, an alchemy system and a substantial bestiary, its rules crunchier than he usually likes. He has already assembled a binder for it, borrowing pages from The Perplexing Ruins campaign notebook.

Death in Space, picked up from a local game store, gets an honest verdict: he enjoys reading it, the binding is so tight the book cracks when opened, and it has not yet inspired him to actually play. He floats pairing it with Cryptic Explorers components, whose art style he thinks matches, and asks whether a dedicated solo system exists for it.

Runecairn Warden Saga arrives via a recommendation from the Stone Axe channel — an expanded Cairn with solo rules baked in and a Dark Souls twist where dying is not the end of the adventure. There is also a stack of Mörk Borg supplements from Exalted Funeral, two zine RPGs, and The Drifter, a print-on-demand wild west game he describes as Barbarian Prince with more variables.

----

Daniel owns books he loves reading and has never played. Where does your own line sit between a game you collect and a game you actually run?
